BETWEEN:-

(BY SHRI RAJNEESH GUPTA - ADVOCATE FOR PETITIONER)
 AND

1. THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH ITS  SECRETARY MANTRALAY BHAWAN BHOPAL  (MADHYA PRADESH)

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
This petition coming on for admission this day, th e cou  following:
 ORDER

This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking following relief(s):-
"It is, therefore, humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to quash the impugned order dated 08.02.2019 (Annexure P-1) and direct the respondents to conduct the spot inspection of the land of the petitioner which has been acquired, as per the order of the concerned Authority under the Right to Information Act dated Ram Ram Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393161/
1 31.10.2018 and determine the compensation for the acquired land as per law and same be paid to the petitioner along with interest from the date of its acquisition in the interest of justice.

entities.text: Ram Ram Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Any other relief(s) which petitioner is found entitled may also be granted to along with exemplary cost all throughout."
2.

It is submitted by counsel for petitioner that petitioner is the owner of Khasra No.338/4/2 area 0.081 hectare and Khasra No.331/C area 0.498 hectare, which is also recorded in the Khasra Panchshala and the respondents without acquiring the land in question have constructed a road over it.

3. The respondents have filed their return and it is submitted by counsel for respondents that it is clear from the impugned order itself that the road was constructed in the year 1971 and it was repaired in the year 1983.
No fresh construction has been raised.

4. In reply, it is submitted by counsel for petitioner that as per Khasra Panchshala, road was mentioned on 08.01.2016, therefore, the contention of the respondents that road is in existence since 1971 is incorrect.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
6.

The constitutional rights of the petitioner cannot be disputed but in the Khasra Panchshala, which has been filed as Annexure P/3, it is specifically mentioned that on 0.021 hectare of Khasra No.338/4/2 and on 0.498 hectare of Khasra No.331/C there is road and the correction was done in the light of order dated 08.01.2016 passed by Tahsildar, Tahsil Raghurajnagar in Revenue Case No.2042A74/2013-14.
7.
Accordingly, counsel for petitioner was directed to point out said order.
8. It is submitted by Shri Gupta that petitioner is not aware of the aforesaid order mentioned in the Khasra Panchshala.
9. So far as the dispute as to whether the road was already in existence from the year 1971 or it has been recently constructed is concerned, the same cannot be decided without recording evidence.
If the petitioner was already dispossessed in the year 1971, then the question of adverse possession against the petitioner may also arise.

Furthermore, the order dated 08.01.2016 passed in Tahsildar,
Raghurajnagar in Revenue Case No.2042A74/2013-14 has neither been challenged nor has been placed on record.
10.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that since multiple disputed questions of facts are involved and the petitioner may also loose his right to take llegal recourse on the basis of adverse possession, the disputed questions cannot be decided by this Court in exercise of power under Article 226 of Constitution of India.

Ram Ram Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44393161/
2 11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner that if so desire, then he may file a civil suit for declaration of possession or compensation in lieu thereof or he may also challenge the order dated 08.01.2016 passed by Tahsildar, Tahsil Raghurajnagar in Revenue Case No.2042A74/2013-14.
12.

It is made clear that this Court has not passed any comment with regard to the ownership of the petitioner and if the civil suit or appeal is filed, then the same shall be decided on their own merits without getting influenced or prejudiced by any part of this order.
(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE VB*
